text:
mo: quick help—customer on macOS can't import our python SDK after `pip install --user redwood-sdk[all]`. They see ModuleNotFoundError even though files are in ~/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages :confused:
user-greg: repro steps i ran on macOS 13.6:
user-greg: `python3 -m pip install --user redwood-sdk[all]==0.9.3`
user-greg: then `python3 -c 'import redwood'` -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'
user-greg: listing site-packages: `ls ~/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages | grep redwood` -> shows redwood_sdk-0.9.3.dist-info and redwood_sdk package dir
mo: probably PATH/python mismatch. Which python is `python3`? `which python3`?
user-greg: `which python3` -> /usr/local/bin/python3 (brew)
user-greg: but VSCode uses /usr/bin/python3? not sure
sara: common mac issue: `pip install --user` install location is tied to the interpreter you ran. Also check `python3 -m site --user-site` to confirm user-site path.
jordan: can you show `python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"` and `python3 -m site` output?
user-greg: pasted outputs: `['', '/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages', '/usr/lib/python3.10', '/Users/greg/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages']` and `USER_BASE: '/Users/greg/.local' USER_SITE: '/Users/greg/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages'`
mo: so site-packages is on sys.path, but import still fails. Are there multiple installs of the package? `pip show redwood-sdk`
user-greg: `pip show redwood-sdk` -> Name: redwood-sdk
Version: 0.9.3
Location: /Users/greg/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages
Requires: httpx, typing-extensions
mo: what does `python3 -m pip list | grep redwood` show?
user-greg: nothing when run from the same python used in app process (the app uses a venv created by pyenv/venv in the project). Hmm
sara: aha — sounds like they installed into the global user site but the app runs in a project venv that doesn't include user site packages. On mac, if venv was created without --system-site-packages, user-site is not visible. 
jordan: also check Poetry: if project uses poetry, `poetry run python -c 'import sys; print(sys.executable)'` and `poetry show`
user-greg: they said they tried poetry: `poetry add ../local/redwood -E sync` and then `poetry install` but VSCode still couldn't import.
mo: editable/local installs + extras often break when pyproject uses PEP 517 build isolation. If they did `pip install -e .[all]` vs `poetry add /path`, it can lead to different installed names (redwood_sdk vs redwood) — confirm package top-level name.
user-greg: the package dir is `redwood_sdk` (underscore). But their imports expect `import redwood`. Could that be the mismatch?
sara: our SDK exports top-level `redwood` package that wraps redwood_sdk. Historically we added a shim package. If their install put only the internal package (redwood_sdk) without the shim, import fails. That can happen if the wheel build excludes the shim due to MANIFEST/pyproject config.
mo: can you try `python3 -c "import importlib.util, sys; print(importlib.util.find_spec('redwood'))"` and same for `redwood_sdk` to see what is resolvable.
user-greg: find_spec('redwood') -> None, find_spec('redwood_sdk') -> ModuleSpec(name='redwood_sdk', ...)
user-greg: so shim missing.
mo: where did they install from — PyPI or local wheel? Could be a bad sdist on older pip or editable install path. Also extras sometimes change which packages are included.
sara: ask user to run `python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip build setuptools wheel` then `python3 -m pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.3` (no --user) inside the venv or `poetry add redwood-sdk@0.9.3` to ensure wheel install with shim present.
jordan: if they need a quick workaround, create a tiny shim in site-packages: `echo "from redwood_sdk import *
from redwood_sdk import __version__ as __version__" > /path/to/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py` but that's a hack.
user-greg: tried `pip install --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir redwood-sdk==0.9.3` inside the project's python and then `python -c 'import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)'` -> ModuleNotFoundError still.
mo: double-check `pip` binary used: `python -m pip show redwood-sdk` vs `pip show redwood-sdk` can differ. Use `python -m pip` to be safe.
user-greg: `python -m pip show redwood-sdk` -> nothing
user-greg: `which pip` -> /usr/local/bin/pip
user-greg: their venv's python executable path is /Users/greg/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/proj-py3.10/bin/python
sara: so the steps: (1) activate the poetry venv or `poetry run python -m pip install redwood-sdk` (2) avoid `--user` when in venv (3) prefer `poetry add redwood-sdk` so poetry manages the dependency.
mo: also check for import name collisions: if a file named redwood.py exists in project root it will shadow package. `ls -la | grep redwood`
user-greg: they had a `redwood.py` test file in project root. OMG. That was shadowing.
user-greg: removed the file, now `python -c 'import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)'` -> 0.9.3 :tada:
mo: excellent — very common. Add to documentation troubleshooting FAQ: "module shadowing (redwood.py) and multiple python/pip binaries on macOS".
jordan: logging note: user also reported httpx retry errors earlier — that might be due to mixed httpx versions from other deps. If they see TypeError in transport kwargs, ask for `pip freeze` inside venv and check httpx==0.24.1 compat.
dev-support-bot: install-report uploaded to ticket #INC-1423 (attached pip freeze, sys.path, outputs).
mo: thanks all. Greg, if anything else pop this thread back or open a support ticket with the virtualenv `python -m pip freeze` and `python -c "import sys, pprint; pprint.pprint(sys.path)"` outputs.
user-greg: will do, thanks!
